lede: This week: Netflix's first Brazilian legal drama and a darker-than-expected Italian teen mystery headline the new arrivals, a French true-crime sensation and Apple's bleak dispatcher thriller round out the under-the-radar catches, and an announced slate topped by Ben Affleck's kidnapping thriller and a Friday the 13th prequel series.

shortlist.title: Habeas Corpus
shortlist.meta: With Marjorie Estiano, Any Gabrielly. Netflix Brazil's first legal drama. Season 1, 8 episodes.
shortlist.blurb: A law professor leading a wrongful-conviction review team fights to free a young man convicted of a crime he says he didn't commit, in Netflix Brazil's first legal drama, inspired by Innocence Project Brazil.

shortlist.title: Physical 100: Italy
shortlist.meta: With Olympians Federica Pellegrini, Jury Chechi, Tania Cagnotto among 100 competitors. Season 1, weekly episodes.
shortlist.blurb: The Italian spinoff of the brutal elimination competition Ian already loved pits 100 competitors, including Olympic champions, through grueling physical challenges for a shot at the top prize.

shortlist.title: Minerva Academy
shortlist.meta: Dir. Ciro Minopoli. Season 1, 8 episodes, all released together.
shortlist.blurb: A seemingly ordinary military-style Naples high school drama turns considerably darker as hazing, abuse of power, and a cadet's disappearance take over the story.
shortlist.tag: Italian teen drama, darker than it looks

shortlist.title: Stop! That! Train!
shortlist.meta: Dir. Adam Shankman; with Ginger Minj, Jujubee. 92 min.
shortlist.blurb: Drag stars Ginger Minj and Jujubee play train stewardesses whose glitzy new gig on the "Glamazonian Express" collides with a catastrophic "Stormaganza" in this gleefully campy disaster-movie spoof.

movies.title: The Last Voyage of the Demeter
movies.blurb: André Øvredal's gothic maritime Dracula horror — the doomed voyage of the Demeter, stalked and slaughtered one by one by an ancient vampire — finds a new streaming home.

tv.title: Sambre
tv.blurb: From the Oscar-winning director of The Staircase, this record-breaking French limited series tracks the decades-long failure to connect a serial rapist to attacks along the same river, through to the #MeToo era.

tv.title: Last Seen
tv.blurb: An alcoholic ex-cop turned 911 dispatcher gets a call that might be about his daughter, missing for 11 years, in a genre-bending psychological thriller critics say "never plays by the rules."

catalog.title: Blue Velvet
catalog.blurb: David Lynch's noir-tinged neo-classic returns to Criterion Channel in a new edition, following Dennis Hopper's psychotic Frank Booth into the underbelly of small-town America.

catalog.title: Thief
catalog.blurb: Michael Mann's stylish directorial debut stars James Caan as a professional safecracker trying to go straight, joining Criterion's library.

catalog.title: The Man Who Fell to Earth
catalog.blurb: Nicolas Roeg's trippy sci-fi classic stars David Bowie as a humanoid alien stranded on Earth, back on Criterion after being out of print.

catalog.title: Pitfall
catalog.blurb: The first entry in Hiroshi Teshigahara's acclaimed collaboration with novelist Kobo Abe, a genre-bending ghost story about a murdered miner, returns to Criterion.

catalog.title: Woman in the Dunes
catalog.blurb: Teshigahara's Cannes-winning existentialist classic, about a man trapped in a sand pit with a mysterious woman, rejoins the Criterion Channel.

catalog.title: The Face of Another
catalog.blurb: The third Teshigahara-Abe collaboration follows a disfigured man given a lifelike mask, rounding out Criterion's retrospective.

catalog.title: Blood for Dracula
catalog.blurb: Paul Morrissey's cult horror-comedy, paired with companion film Flesh for Frankenstein, returns to streaming as part of Criterion's cult classics slate.

catalog.title: Bad Lieutenant
catalog.blurb: Harvey Keitel's unhinged, unredeemable cop anchors Abel Ferrara's grimy NYC classic, part of a full 19-film Ferrara retrospective now on Criterion.

announced.title: Animals
announced.blurb: Ben Affleck writes, directs, and stars as an LA mayoral candidate whose family is targeted by kidnappers in this Taken-meets-The Town thriller, co-starring Kerry Washington and Steven Yeun; Netflix dropped the full trailer this week.

announced.title: The Trap
announced.blurb: Netflix confirmed an Oct. 13 date for this German psychological thriller adapting Melanie Raabe's novel, starring Friederike Becht as a reclusive author using herself as bait to catch her sister's killer.

announced.title: Crystal Lake
announced.blurb: Peacock's A24-produced Friday the 13th prequel series, starring Linda Cardellini as young Pam Voorhees, dropped its trailer and confirmed all 8 episodes arrive Oct. 15.

announced.title: Doctor X
announced.blurb: Netflix confirmed Kim Ji-won's medical-thriller K-drama streams day-and-date with its Korean broadcast starting Oct. 9.

announced.title: Dead-End Job
announced.blurb: Netflix set an Oct. 30 date for this fantasy-horror-mystery K-drama starring Lee Jae-wook, Go Min-si, and Kim Min-ha — a sharper genre swing than the usual rom-com K-drama slate.

announced.title: The Remarried Empress
announced.blurb: Disney+ confirmed a Nov. 4 premiere for this lavish webtoon-adapted fantasy-romance K-drama starring Shin Min-ah, Ju Ji-hoon, and Lee Jong-suk.

announced.title: Tenzing
announced.blurb: Apple confirmed an Oct. 16 streaming date for this Sherpa mountaineering drama, following a brief theatrical run.

announced.title: Small Prophets
announced.blurb: Apple TV confirmed an Oct. 7 premiere for Mackenzie Crook's (Detectorists) new comedy about a man who learns to create fortune-telling spirits — the acclaimed BBC series holds a perfect 100% on Rotten Tomatoes.

announced.title: Mononoke the Movie: Chapter III – The Curse of the Serpent
announced.blurb: Netflix confirmed the trilogy finale of its acclaimed Ōoku-set supernatural-mystery anime lands globally Sept. 29.

announced.title: Red River
announced.blurb: Crunchyroll confirmed the shoujo-isekai adaptation's second cour, set in the Hittite Empire, returns Sept. 29 with new cast additions including Nana Mizuki.
